notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Jeremiah 17 this time, because I wasn't able to read any of the approved sources.

My first try at fetching four pages crashed: Enduring Word, the Bible Hub commentaries on 17:9, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. It failed on how I read the results, before I could see anything on the pages. After that I hit the tool's usage limit, so I couldn't retry or run any searches. Your rules say not to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written notes on any verse.

If you ask again in a new message, the tools should be available again. I'd begin with these pages, which are likely to give verse-by-verse comment:
- **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word's Jeremiah 17 commentary, plus Bible Hub and StudyLight pages per verse (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry). The verses I'd look at most closely are 1, 5–8, 9–10, 11, 13 and 21–27.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
  - Verse 9 ("the heart is deceitful"): Reformed and Baptist teaching on total depravity (Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY) against Wesleyan teaching on grace that comes before faith (Wesley's notes at wesley.nnu.edu, Seedbed).
  - Verses 19–27 (the Sabbath): how Reformed, Lutheran and other teachers apply the Sabbath command today (Ligonier, LCMS, 1517, GotQuestions).
- **Other views:**
  - The NET Bible notes on wording questions, for example "beyond cure" in v. 9 and the partridge in v. 11.
  - Bible Odyssey on Asherah (v. 2) and on how the Sabbath passage relates to the rest of Jeremiah.
  - Catholic and Orthodox readings of verses 5–8 from the Church Fathers (New Advent, Catholic.com, OCA).
  - Possibly prosperity or word-of-faith uses of verses 7–8, if the approved sites discuss them.
